name: OpenOnload (with ef_vi and TCPDirect kernel-bypass APIs)
listed_description: Solarflare kernel-bypass user-space network stack and APIs (OpenOnload, ef_vi, TCPDirect) that skip system calls and buffer copies on supported NICs; Exablaze NICs are named as another kernel-bypass option.
claim_text: Kernel bypass offers a low-latency path that avoids system calls and buffer copies; no numbers given.
found_in: book: Building Low Latency Applications with C++ (2023), ch. 2, Exploring low latency electronic trading, Network Interface Cards, switches, and kernel bypass

name: Book MemPool: single-vector object-plus-free-flag preallocated pool
listed_description: Template object pool in Chapter4/mem_pool.h that preallocates one vector of blocks, each holding the object and its free flag, and serves allocations with placement new instead of heap calls.
claim_text: Pre-allocating at startup and serving out memory at runtime performs significantly better than dynamic allocation; storing flag beside object is better for cache.
book_benchmark: Chunk gives design only, no timings; benchmark against heap allocation is in a later chapter of the book (see other chunks).
found_in: book: Building Low Latency Applications with C++ (2023), ch. 4, Designing C++ memory pools to avoid dynamic memory allocations

name: Book CRTP compile-time polymorphism for order placement
listed_description: Chapter3/crtp.cpp replaces virtual-function runtime polymorphism with the Curiously Recurring Template Pattern so calls resolve at compile time and can inline.
claim_text: Templates remove runtime overhead and unlock additional compiler optimization opportunities, at cost of code complexity and larger executables.
book_benchmark: No timings; example only prints which override ran.
found_in: book: Building Low Latency Applications with C++ (2023), ch. 3, Using compile-time polymorphism

name: Book branchless side-indexed fill update
listed_description: Chapter3/branch.cpp updates trading position and last buy/sell quantity by casting the buy/sell enum to an integer index into an array, avoiding an if/else branch.
book_benchmark: No timings; only checks both versions compute the same values.
found_in: book: Building Low Latency Applications with C++ (2023), ch. 3, Maximizing C++ compiler optimization parameters, Minimizing branching
